events.title: Iran war: Hormuz tanker attacks and Gulf strikes push Brent to six-month high (peak ~$117, 30 Oct), then retreat on ceasefire talks
events.description: The US/Israel-Iran war (running since roughly Feb-Mar 2026 per Aug 2026 'after 6 months of war' coverage) re-escalated in Oct 2026: IRGC-claimed tanker fires/mines on the Hormuz route (11 tankers in 9 days per IRGC-linked report), Houthi strikes on Saudi Arabia, Brent briefly >$117 on 30 Oct. From 2 Nov Brent fell sharply (steepest weekly loss since 2022) on a draft US-Iran ceasefire proposal; Tehran called it 'insufficient' on 3 Nov. Hormuz crude flows had largely recovered to pre-war levels by 1 Oct (Guardian). Brent quotes in news differ by contract/date (4 Nov: $90-104 across outlets); the model uses the factor_state close.
events.what_already_moved: factor_state 2026-11-05: Brent 94.99 (1m -5.6%, 3m +15.2%, 12m +49.5%, flat since 1 Jun); refining margin +15.4% since 1 Jun; USD/INR 94.49 (rupee had neared record low ~96 in Sep-Oct, RBI hiked repo to 5.50% on 7 Oct); FPI equity outflows Rs ~3 lakh cr in CY26 (Rs 48,056 cr in Oct to 25 Oct); India VIX 15.3 (3m +26%).

entry_shocks.note: escalation already priced in part; now partly unwound

chains.explanation: India imports ~85% of crude; higher Brent widens CAD and weakens INR (rupee near 96).
Oil and fuel pass-through lift CPI; RBI hiked 25 bp on 7 Oct and flagged more.
Wide cracks help export refiners; higher feedstock costs hurt OMC marketing margins (HINDPETRO).
Risk-off raises VIX and FPI selling, pressuring high-beta midcaps.

most_affected_hint.why: regulated retail prices compress marketing margin when crude is high

events.title: US 60-day waiver of Russia sanctions law / 100% secondary-tariff threat on buyers of Russian oil (India)
events.description: In Sep 2026 Trump signed a Russia sanctions law (Graham bill) letting the US tariff buyers of Russian oil up to 100%. On ~17 Oct he waived it for 60 days (Rubio: a pause to analyse global impact; India 'cannot stop buying overnight'). India's Russian crude imports stabilised ~1.8-1.9 mb/d; total crude imports hit record 5.4-5.6 mb/d in Oct with UAE/Venezuelan/US diversification. Waiver lapses around mid-Dec 2026 unless extended.
events.what_already_moved: No tariff imposed. Russian crude discount and Indian refiners' access preserved; Brent not materially moved by it (flat since 1 Jun).

entry_shocks.note: access preserved vs a threatened loss
removal of a tail 100% threat (SSU = +10pp avg tariff)

chains.explanation: Discounted Russian barrels sustain refiners' margins.
Avoiding loss of ~1.8 mb/d prevents a Brent spike and CPI pass-through.
Lower tariff-tail risk supports INR and FPI sentiment.

most_affected_hint.why: Jamnagar Russian-crude flexibility (export product sanctions caveat)
less tariff-risk premium on India exporters

events.title: US Section 232 pharma tariff (100%) takes effect 29 Sep 2026; select Indian speciality drugs/ingredients exempted

In July Trump had threatened a 200% tariff on generics; generics so far not hit (Indian firms argue US needs low-cost generics). Sun Pharma reportedly offered cheaper drugs to the administration (MFN-style pricing deals). Exact HS scope of exemptions and generics treatment not verified from primary text.

entry_shocks.note: branded/speciality tariff in force with India carve-outs; generics spared (SSU=+10pp on Indian pharma exports; effective average small)

chains.explanation: Tariff on competitors' branded products and MFN deals shift US pricing power; generic price erosion pressure persists.
Speciality-heavy exporters (Sun, Lupin, Zydus) carry the exemption-dependency risk.

events.title: India-US interim trade agreement formally signed/announced
events.description: Talks have repeatedly 'stalled' (Reuters 6 Oct) yet US officials say '98-99% done' (16 Oct), Trump says 'pretty close, different from previous pacts' (21 Oct), and the White House already lists an India deal among 'promises kept' (3 Nov) without a signed text. A 'forward MFN' clause is under discussion. Hurdles: agriculture/dairy, Russian oil, US wanting competitor-country tariffs first (The Hindu 22 Sep). A narrow interim deal is the modal outcome. Midterm result may reduce US urgency or raise it. Current effective US tariff level on India is not verified from a primary source (legal basis shifted after a SCOTUS ruling; Greer says policy 'hasn't changed').
